monument_name: Bhurtī group of three śikharas (13th-15th cent.)
description_en: Three śikhara temples from approximately 13th-15th century.The monuments are found in the southern part of the Bhurtī Temple Complex. The site itself is located in the northern end of the settlement of Bhurtī, 3 km north of Narayana, the district headquarters. It currently comprises 22 standingśikharatemples (ordevala) and one stone fountain. Architectural activity at the site can be situated between the 13thand 15thcentury, a time period corresponding to the latter part of the Khaśa Malla empire and the early phase of the Rāskoṭi dynasty (Andolfatto 2019,Pokharel 2011: 128-129,Sharma 1972: 23-31,Sharma 2012: 120-123).In 2008, the “Bhurti Temple Complex of Dailekh” was enlisted on UNESCO’s World Heritage Tentative List by the Government of Nepal (criteriaiiandiv).The monuments are organised around one centralśikharatemple (001), oriented to the south. The two otherśikharasare oriented towards the latter. Only the central temple has its original āmalaka ring on top. The northern temple has a recently made one and the southern one has none. It seems that the central temple was rebuilt, as indicated by numbers marked on the stone masonry.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired), Rebuilt

Paris: Sorbonne Université. Pokharel, Bishwo K. C. 2011. Kīrtikhamba . Kathmandu: Prakāśka. Sharma, P. R. 1972. Preliminary Study of the Art and Architecture of the Karnali Basin, West Nepal. Paris: CNRS. Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.
